tags: Jump stop · late in a decided game · injury-interrupted season
what_happened: Late in a playoff opener his team led by 12, Rose drove the lane, jump-stopped as two defenders rotated over, changed his mind and passed, and came down awkwardly on the left leg. No contact was described.
context: He had missed 27 regular-season games to injuries that season, so the knee was carrying a playoff workload after a stop-start year.
prevention_angle: Jump stops are one of the three most common ACL situations in NBA video. Deceleration and landing mechanics (knee over toes, avoiding inward collapse) are trainable. Minutes in a decided game are a coaching choice.

tags: Push-off from planted foot · very high recent minutes · age 34
what_happened: Driving toward the basket late in a close game, Bryant pushed off his planted left foot in a routine move and went down without contact. He stayed in to make two free throws.
context: Reporting at the time noted he had averaged nearly 46 minutes over the previous seven games during a playoff push. He had also hyperextended the same knee earlier that night.
prevention_angle: This fits the classic NBA Achilles pattern: non-contact take-off with rapid ankle dorsiflexion. A sustained spike above the player's normal minutes is the kind of signal a monitoring system should flag.

phase: Landing after contact in the air
tags: Mid-air collision · first minutes of the season
what_happened: Minutes into his Celtics debut, Hayward went up for a lob, collided with LeBron James in mid-air, and landed awkwardly on his leg.
context: It was the season opener, so there was no in-season workload story. This was a traumatic, contact-driven injury.
prevention_angle: Largely not preventable through training. Landing after mid-air contact is a high-risk situation. Bodyweight-bearing landing practice (falling and rolling safely) can lower the odds of the worst outcomes.

phase: Explosive first step to a rebound
tags: Heavy big · chasing a rebound · non-contact
what_happened: In the fourth quarter he went for a rebound off a missed free throw and came up limping. No contact was involved.
context: He was one of the league's heaviest high-minute players. His recent games ran several minutes above his season average (see figures).
prevention_angle: Heavy, high-usage bigs carry more load per step through the calf-Achilles unit. Eccentric calf strength and forefoot acceleration training are the countermeasures the video research points to.

tags: Very tall player · single-leg landing after dunking over a defender
what_happened: In the second quarter he drove and dunked over Giannis Antetokounmpo, then came down awkwardly on his left leg.
context: At 7-foot-3 he was in the tallest tier of players in the dataset. The landing was on one leg.
prevention_angle: Landing after contact in the air is the second most common NBA ACL situation. Two-foot landing habits and strength to control valgus (knee caving inward) are the trainable parts.

tags: First game back after a same-leg calf strain · long layoff · Finals intensity
what_happened: In his first game back, he went down on a crossover on the right wing in the second quarter, grabbing the back of his lower leg after 12 minutes.
context: He had strained his right calf in the conference finals and missed over a month. Game 5 of the Finals was his return.
prevention_angle: A recent calf strain on the same leg, followed by a return straight into peak intensity, is the risk pattern now under study in the NBA. Graded return-to-play loading and objective calf-strength benchmarks before clearance are the levers.

tags: Fouled in the air on a breakaway · 100th game of the season
what_happened: Late in the third quarter of Finals Game 6, Danny Green fouled him on a breakaway dunk attempt and he landed awkwardly. He shot his free throws, then left.
context: It was his 100th game of the season including playoffs, and his recent minutes were well above his regular-season average.
prevention_angle: Landing after contact is the hardest situation to train away. Cumulative playoff load is a monitored risk factor, not a cause on its own.

phase: Landing on an opponent's foot during a drive
tags: Euro step · foul on the drive · foot landed on a defender's foot
what_happened: Fouled on a Euro-step drive, his right foot came down on a defender's foot. He lost balance and landed awkwardly on his left leg, with the knee appearing to hyperextend.
context: He stayed in to make both free throws before leaving. This is an in-season, mid-game injury on a drive.
prevention_angle: Driving into a crowded lane with defenders' feet under you is the textbook setup for both ankle sprains and indirect-contact ACL tears. Reactive balance and landing training target the recovery step.

tags: Third game back after a month out · chasing a long rebound
what_happened: Chasing an offensive rebound after a missed three, he collapsed grabbing his left calf and Achilles area and could not bear weight.
context: He had missed over a month with a blood clot in his right calf and had returned only two games earlier in the series.
prevention_angle: This is a return from a long layoff straight into playoff intensity. Re-conditioning time after any extended absence is a modifiable factor.

phase: Sudden change of direction for a loose ball
tags: Loose ball · step back and re-accelerate · very heavy playoff minutes
what_happened: Going after a loose ball late in the fourth quarter, he stepped back on his right leg and collapsed with no contact.
context: His recent playoff minutes were far above his regular-season average (see figures). He played 40 minutes in this game.
prevention_angle: Late-game, high-minute, explosive direction changes match both the Achilles video pattern and the short-term workload rise reported before NBA ruptures.

tags: Playing through a same-leg calf strain · Game 7 of the Finals
what_happened: In the first quarter of Finals Game 7 he went down without contact while driving to the basket.
context: He had strained his right calf earlier in the series and played through it after passing mobility tests.
prevention_angle: A same-leg calf strain shortly before rupture repeats the Durant pattern. A 2026 study examines prior calf strain as an Achilles risk factor in NBA players. Experts at the time said the link was not yet established.
